g.title: vllm_rust_frontend
g.text: vLLM Rust Frontend (rust/src) — crates and the Python modules they replace

g.title: cluster_pycore
g.text: Python engine core — NOT replaced, runs as a child process

g.title: cluster_modes
g.text: Startup modes — who is the parent process

g.title: cluster_pybridge
g.text: Reverse bridge — Python calls into Rust in-process

g.title: cluster_bench
g.text: Separate program — load generator, NOT part of vllm-rs

g.title: cmd
g.text: CLI entry + arg repartition (Rust-owned flags vs Python passthrough),
no Python counterpart — it is the process Python's cli/serve.py would fork

g.title: server
g.text: LoRA, dev routes — plus auth / CORS / request-id / load middleware and a gRPC sidecar

g.title: chat
g.text: renderer selection, structured assistant event stream

g.title: text
g.text: prompt lowering + sampling params, incremental detokenization,
logprob / prompt-logprob decode, HF tokenizer+config loading

g.title: pybridge
g.text: the ONLY PyO3 extension in the workspace

g.title: ecc
g.text: ZMQ + MessagePack wire protocol, handshake, request routing,
output demux, DP coordinator, utility RPC

g.title: metrics
g.text: Prometheus registry: scheduler / request / http families

g.title: zmq
g.text: transport: ROUTER (requests in) / PULL (outputs out) / DEALER (handshake)
handshake: HELLO to INIT to READY to EngineCoreReadyResponse

g.title: modeA
g.text: Python binds the listen socket, starts EngineCore,
then spawns `vllm-rs frontend` as a supervised worker
handing it the inherited fd (--listen-fd) and the

g.title: modeC
g.text: Rust frontend only; the Python engine

g.title: modeB
g.text: Rust binds its own listener and spawns

g.title: managed
g.text: port allocation, process-group SIGTERM to SIGKILL

g.title: mock
g.text: protocol-level fake engine (no GPU, no Python)
Rust-only test double, no Python counterpart

g.title: bench_rs
g.text: standalone binary, no Python at runtime
